title: Classical multidimensional scaling
code_simulate:
set.seed(240511)
ecotype <- rep(c("Forest", "Grassland", "Dune"), each=25)
size <- rnorm(75, rep(c(12,14,13),each=25), 1.2)
d <- data.frame(ecotype, body_mm=size,
  wing_mm=1.3*size+rnorm(75,0,1), femur_mm=.45*size+rnorm(75,0,.4),
  antenna_mm=.7*size+rep(c(0,1,-1),each=25)+rnorm(75,0,.5))
write.csv(d, file.path(out_dir, "data.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
code_plot:
coordinates <- result$points
colours <- c("#146A85", "#C56B3B", "#5B8266")[match(d$ecotype,c("Forest","Grassland","Dune"))]
plot(coordinates, pch=21, bg=colours, cex=1.1, asp=1,
     xlab="Dimension 1", ylab="Dimension 2")
legend("topright", c("Forest","Grassland","Dune"), pch=21,
       pt.bg=c("#146A85", "#C56B3B", "#5B8266"), bty="n")
code_analysis:
z <- scale(d[c("body_mm","wing_mm","femur_mm","antenna_mm")])
distance <- dist(z)
result <- cmdscale(distance, k=2, eig=TRUE)
biology: Four correlated morphological traits are measured in beetles from three ecotypes.
design: 25 independent beetles per ecotype; four traits on each individual.
question: Can a low-dimensional map preserve the chosen between-individual distances?
null: The target is a low-dimensional configuration that preserves the chosen distances; this map is not itself a hypothesis test.
options: Choose and justify the distance measure.
Inspect representation quality, not just separation.
assumptions: The chosen distance represents biological similarity.
A 2D view may distort higher-dimensional distances.
parametric: Use a model that directly tests the biological group contrast if inference is the aim.
nonparametric: Consider rank- or distance-based approaches when their target matches the question.
generating_model: 75 beetles: 25 per ecotype. Body size is Normal(mean 12,14,13 mm by Forest,Grassland,Dune; SD 1.2). Wing=1.3×size+Normal(0,1); femur=0.45×size+Normal(0,0.4); antenna=0.7×size+ecotype shift(0,1,−1)+Normal(0,0.5). All errors independent.
generating_truth: Groups differ in body-size means and antenna shifts; all traits share a common body-size component.
teaching_point: Distance choice defines what counts as similar.

plot_args.note: Shows known ecotypes with outlined colors
Keeps one coordinate unit the same size on both axes

practice: What biological claim would this plot alone fail to establish?
